text:
Maria (CSM): Quick heads-up — PulseMed goes GA next week. They want explicit SLO acceptance before go-live: uptime 99.9% (monthly) and p95 latency <= 200ms for their tokenized embed endpoints. Also asked how latency credits would be calculated if we miss. Can SRE/SE confirm feasibility and the credit calc? @Sam @Dave
Sam (Solutions Eng): High-level: hosted can meet 99.9% and 200ms p95 but for production traffic I recommend Dedicated with prefix KV caching. Need a 30-day acceptance window and realistic traffic profile from the customer. Drafted an SLO YAML snippet for the acceptance packet:
```yaml
service: pulsemed-embed
slo:
  - name: uptime
    target: 0.999
    window: 30d
  - name: p95_latency_ms
    target: 200
    percentile: 95
```
Sam (Solutions Eng): For credits, we usually do: credit_fraction = max(0, (target - observed) / target). credit_amount = min(credit_fraction * monthly_commit, cap). Need to confirm monetary conversion/cap with finance and CS policy.
Dave (SRE): A couple of operational caveats: p95 200ms assumes moderate sequence lengths (~512 tokens) and batching. If they send long sequences (1k-2k) RPS per node drops significantly and p95 will increase. Cold KV/prefix cache causes spikes during day 0; we should require a warm-up run in the acceptance plan. Recommend canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%).
Dave (SRE): Suggested fallback behavior (informal): if p95 > 250ms sustained for 5m AND error_rate < 0.5% then route to model-variant-small and trigger incident alert; capture decision time and annotate customer report.
Olivia (CS Ops): I'll capture these operational assumptions in the SLO acceptance packet: warm-up steps, expected seq lengths, canary schedule, fallback policy, and a link to the warm-up playground. Also adding an evidence checklist (latency graphs, KV hit-rate, canary logs).
Olivia (CS Ops): Can SE add expected steady-state RPS per node for sizing Dedicated? Need conservative numbers for the packet.
Sam (Solutions Eng): Rough sizing: for A100-ish nodes with batching and 512 tokens we see ~80-120 RPS; for ~2k tokens expect ~30-50 RPS. I'll add a conservative table to the packet showing RPS by token length and recommended node counts for sample commit sizes.
Elaine (Enablement): PulseMed requested a 45-min enablement for their SRE/dev team to cover SLO reporting, what triggers credits, and runbook playthrough. Can we do Wed 10am PT? I'll record and share materials.
Maria (CSM): Wed 10am PT works. Action items: 
- [ ] SE: finalize SLO YAML and insert RPS sizing table (Sam)
- [ ] SRE: finalize fallback wording, warm-up checklist, and worked credit example (Dave)
- [ ] CS Ops: assemble acceptance packet + runbook link + evidence checklist (Olivia)
- [ ] Enablement: schedule and record the enablement session (Elaine)
- [ ] CSM: send acceptance packet to PulseMed and capture signed acceptance (Maria)
Sam (Solutions Eng): Draft uploaded internally: https://redwood-internal.notebooks/slo/pulsemed-draft — please review and comment before EOD.
deploy-bot: Automated notice: Canary deploy for pulsemed-embed scheduled 2024-07-18T18:00Z (job #78912).
Dave (SRE): For transparency on credit calc, we'll include a worked numeric example in the packet. Example: target 99.9% -> observed 99.6% -> outage_fraction = 0.0003 -> credit_fraction = outage_fraction/0.001 = 0.3 -> if monthly_commit = $20k then credit = $6k (subject to cap). I'll coordinate with finance to confirm the $/uptime conversion.
Olivia (CS Ops): I'll add that worked example and mark the packet with 'illustrative only' until finance confirms final numbers.
Maria (CSM): Please tag this item for the renewal-risk review in Q4 — we want to correlate any early reliability issues to renewal signals. Once Olivia posts the packet I'll send to the customer for signature and close this thread. Thanks all :thumbsup:
